author: claude
author_note: Authored by a Claude-family model (the same family as the evaluated agents); see CASES.md. Grading has two parts: key/hidden.test.mjs against the delivered accordion.mjs + accordion.css (7 tests), and these detectors against the report.
severity_rubric: R5 applied to a component: critical = the component's primary task fails for some users (keyboard users cannot reach a header; panels cannot be hidden); major = measurable harm to access or correctness; minor = polish.

defects.title: In single mode toggle() appends the new id to the open list instead of replacing it, so the previously open panel stays open and two panels are expanded.
defects.evidence: toggle: const open = [...state.open.filter((x) => x !== id), id]; the allowMultiple branch was lost in the r214 refactor, so single mode behaves like multiple mode (public test 'single mode closes the previously open panel' fails with open ['a', 'b']).
defects.fix: Return open: state.allowMultiple ? [...state.open.filter((x) => x !== id), id] : [id].
defects.rationale: The public test names the symptom, so most agents find it; the detector checks that the report names the cause in toggle (the lost allowMultiple branch), not a patch elsewhere.

detector.example: 1. [major] [code] toggle() in single mode appends the new id instead of replacing the open list, so the previously open panel stays open.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: moveFocus('End') sets focus to items.length, an index past the last header, so keyboard users pressing End lose focus (criterion: primary task fails for keyboard users).
defects.evidence: case 'End': return { ...state, focus: n }; the demo then calls querySelectorAll('.acc-btn')[n]?.focus() on undefined.
defects.rationale: An off-by-one on a rarely used key; ArrowDown and Home are correct, which the brief's false hint about ArrowDown is meant to distract from.

any: End[^\n]{0,80}(off.by.one|items\.length|n - 1|n-1|past the last|out of (range|bounds)|one too far|undefined)
detector.example: 2. [critical] [a11y] moveFocus('End') returns focus: n (items.length), one past the last header, so End drops keyboard focus.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: renderHtml sets aria-controls to acc-panel-{index} while the panel id is acc-panel-{id}, so each button references a panel that does not exist.
defects.rationale: aria-labelledby on the panel is correct, so the markup looks consistent at a glance; only the button side uses the index.

detector.example: 3. [major] [a11y] aria-controls uses the array index (acc-panel-0) while the panel id uses the item id (acc-panel-a), so the reference is broken.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: The rule .acc .acc-panel { display:block } ties the specificity of .acc-panel[hidden] and comes later, so hidden panels are displayed and the accordion cannot collapse (criterion: primary task fails).
defects.evidence: .acc-panel[hidden] { display:none } (0,2,0) is followed by .acc .acc-panel { display:block } (0,2,0); the later rule wins.
defects.fix: Drop display from the .acc .acc-panel rule (or scope it as .acc-panel and keep display out of it), as SPEC.md requires.
defects.rationale: The CSS regression is outside the JS test file, so an agent that only runs tests misses why the demo shows every panel open.

detector.example: 4. [critical] [code] .acc .acc-panel { display:block } has the same specificity as .acc-panel[hidden] and comes later, so hidden panels still display.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.

defects.title: renderHtml escapes the content but not the title, so a title containing markup or quotes is injected unescaped (SPEC: both are escaped).
defects.evidence: >${item.title} versus >${esc(item.content)}; no public test covers it.
defects.rationale: Not covered by the public tests and not mentioned in the brief; only a reading of SPEC.md against the code reveals it.

detector.example: 5. [major] [code] renderHtml escapes item.content but inserts item.title raw, contrary to SPEC.md, so markup in a title is injected.
detector.note: Match the described effect, not a file-name list. Spans use [^\n] (not [^.\n]) so file names with dots inside a one-line finding do not break a match.
